title: Grimaud, castle, lanes and hill village
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The old village of Grimaud deserves to be approached for itself. Its castle, lanes and higher viewpoints provide a clear reading of the commune before the plain and Port Grimaud.
content:
Grimaud is often mentioned together with its opening towards the sea, yet the reading begins higher up. The castle, old streets and viewpoints of the village give the walk a strong framework.

The castle puts the commune back into perspective

From the heights, the site logic becomes clear at once. The castle matters not only for its silhouette; it also explains the relation between defence, control of relief and the reading of the plain.

The lanes keep a Provençal measure

The old village remains habitable in its proportions. Its passages, small squares and level changes preserve a simple density without forced monumentality. That accuracy is what gives the walk its quality.

Why it helps to start here before going down

Starting from the old hill village makes it easier to understand afterwards the plain, wet sectors and the opening towards Port Grimaud. Without this first level of height, the commune looks more fragmented than it really is.

This note extends the page Walking Through Grimaud. To continue within the same cluster, it also helps to open Grimaud between Port Grimaud, the plain and water landscapes.
